claims.text: Mandatory human approval before a healed locator persists is already documented by Katalon and Testsigma; Falcon's approval gate alone is not a differentiator.

Tricentis Testim documents a numeric locator score with an acted-on threshold (70%), so scoring itself is not unique to Falcon. Whether Testim shows that number to a user was not found in the reviewed page, which is not evidence either way and must not be read as Falcon being alone in displaying one.

Virtuoso QA is the closest documented analogue to Falcon's intended trust model: it implements both a confidence threshold gating automatic application and an explicit human Accept/Reject path, though it never shows the numeric score to users.
Momentic already separates a run-scoped repair (never edits the test) from a persisted repair (triage); this conceptual split is not unique to Falcon, though the persistence mechanism differs.
Historical repository adoption measurements were not reproducible from committed responses and are withdrawn. Healenium Pro publicly documents Playwright Proxy.
mabl technical documentation is accessible as of 2026-10-05 and documents environment-specific models, low-confidence failure, conditional automatic persistence and rollback.

BrowserStack's publicly cited "40% reduction in automation build failures" figure is an unqualified vendor press claim with no stated methodology, population, or time period, and does not appear on BrowserStack's own technical documentation; it must never be used as a benchmark baseline or comparison target.
